correctness.rationale: For all fixed 0<a<b, d>0 and every h>0, direct differentiation gives the time-changed Lotka--Volterra equations and the conserved strictly convex separated Hamiltonian. Each positive level is a periodic oval. The exact original-time branch density has inverse-root endpoint singularities. On both outer W regions the Jacobian |dW/dq| is <=2/(b-a); on the central W interval q=h-O(1). These yield an O(log(2+h)) L1 bound for density excess, an h/(b-a)+O(log h) normalization, a period h/(abd)+O(log h), and total variation O(log h/h) under the reciprocal-to-Pareto mapping. The negative-V branch carries probability 1-O(log h/h), giving extinction-boundary concentration. Exact logarithmic period balances give nonzero time means. The included symbolic and quadrature code ran successfully, without substituting finite experiments for the limit proof.

value.rationale: A natural chemical center gives long-period oscillations near its extinction boundary. The quantified original-time Pareto law controls the complete distribution of first-species concentration and exposes a rare-spike discrepancy between typical vanishing concentrations and persistent exact positive means. This supplies structural dynamical information not equivalent to a known center or an orbit-period computation. The specified observable is chemically intrinsic and the error bound is for all measurable events, not a one-off numerical slice.
